title: AC Conductivity and Dielectric Constant of Fast Ion-Electronic Conductor AgI-C
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    The conductivity, dielectric constant and crystal structure of the superionic-electronic conductor AgI-porous carbon composites have been investigated at various temperatures and carbon concentrations (
                    <jats:italic>ϕ</jats:italic>
                    ≤ 10%). At a fixed temperature, both conductivity and dielectric constant exhibit anomalous variation with
                    <jats:italic>ϕ</jats:italic>
                    showing maxima of the values. We observed significant differences in the behavior between the superionic (
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                    ) phase and insulating (
                    <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                    ) phase. By incorporating carbon, the conductivity increases by four times in the
                    <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                    phase and six times in the
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                    phase whereas the dielectric constant increases by five times and eight times respectively. Unlike in the
                    <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                    phase, the conductivity of the
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                    phase exhibits two distinct maxima whereas the dielectric constant exhibits different features of the profiles in different frequency regions in the
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                    phase. Also, the peak value of these properties exhibits power-law dependence on the frequency in both phases but with different values for the exponents.
                  </jats:p>
journal: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology
